title: The Goofus Five's curved soprano saxophonist
summary: Waters praises a white curved-soprano player on the Goofus Five records, known only from the pictures, and Schaap guesses it was Bobby Davis.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: You can't tell who's better, they just blowing like hell, that's all. So's I'm not taking anything away from him, I'm not - but for me personally, I like the sound of Johnny in some things better because his tone was more purity for me. But he says himself that it's, he is the first inspiration. It's natural because Sidney's the first one, one of the first ones, to play, to pioneer in the damn soprano saxes. There's another little white boy that was all, that nobody never talks about but me as it seems, but maybe you've heard about him. You ever hear of the Goofus Five?
Sure.
Well, that little saxophone player was playin' the, he was playin' a curved soprano. He was something else in the same period, the Goofus Five -
Right -
I remember now, I mean it's a long time. And I never heard 'em in person.
Um hum.
Benny Waters JOHP 6/6/82
I only heard the records of that group.
Probably one of the people with Kirkeby. Did you know his name at the time?
No.
You just knew that it was a sound on the Goofus Five records?
Yeah, and I know he was playin' like hell on that soprano -
Uh huh -
'cause, you know -
What - you were starting to then expand to listening to more people. In Philadelphia your style was untouched because there was nobody to listen to or copy. Who was -
That's it -
But in Boston -
That's -
You started picking up -
Yeah, pickin' up on the record. You could buy records then, see, you know what I mean?
And you couldn't in Philadelphia in the late 'teens 'cause there weren't records to be bought.
Yeah.
What records were you buying? You mentioned the Clarence Williams Blue Five sides, you mentioned the Goofus Five -
Yeah -
What other records were you getting into?
Oh, the Goofus Five I used to listen to, and they passed me, the Blue Five, now let's see, most -
Was this -
Benny Waters JOHP 6/6/82
Most any record that I could buy from that period, I don't remember -
Do you think it was Rollini on the goofus or Bobby Davis on soprano that was knockin' you out on the Goofus Five, or wouldn't you know?
I don't know the names -
Uh huh -
It wouldn't be Rollini, Rollini's the famed bass saxophone and vibraphone -
Yeah, well the Goofus I guess is just playing the mouthpiece or something, he's -
No, no, no, he was playing soprano saxophone, curved.
Well, if it was curved, you saw the person. That's why I'm -
No, but I know they was curved, I saw the picture -
Oh, I see -
You see what I mean, the record, you know what I mean?
So it's probably Bobby Davis, but it's hard to say.
I don't know their names, see, now I don't have -
You just saw the picture -
Yeah, yeah, it was a curved saxophone.
